context: a single passage from a letter by J. D. Hooker, which you are answering on its own
exchanges: I send by post 2 tracts from A Gray— I cannot follow Dana’s metaphysical ideas on species. What do you say to them

Thanks for Dana’s pamphlet: I am much disappointed in it. I have high respect for Dana, but in this brochure “I do not think he is much of a Baconian philosopher,” as our friend J. E. Gray says.— I hate such far-fetched analogies, as comparing an atom of oxygen with a living being.— I believe, poor fellow, he believes in 1st Chr. of Genesis, so great allowances must be made for him.
